weeks.title: Continue and calibrate
weeks.objective: Carry useful prior-block work into productive training; standardize observations without a beginner reset.
weeks.progression: Retain established doses and variants; calibrate only uncertainty.
weeks.assessment: Comparable opening observations replace some work; actual prior-block history is required for individual continuation.

weeks.title: Repeat and refine
weeks.objective: Make execution repeatable while allowing a single justified strength or range change.
weeks.progression: Stabilize explosive tasks; selected strength changes remain anchor-specific.
weeks.assessment: Record cue effects, usable range and reserve; judge repeatability rather than best-only output.

weeks.title: Develop one demand
weeks.objective: Develop a selected distance, approach, intent, hinge dose or signal-timing demand from demonstrated prerequisites.
weeks.progression: One planned dose/task variable per lead change; preserve recovery and complementary work.
weeks.assessment: Check response after each changed exposure and against adjacent sport/tumbling; hold when only partly ready.

weeks.title: Review and consolidate
weeks.objective: Compare known tasks and identify what to retain or develop in the next emphasis period.
weeks.progression: Comparable observation, retention or justified reduction; no forced universal deload.
weeks.assessment: Review work replaces training work; record productive dose separately from a lighter review dose.

weeks.title: Restore and direct force
weeks.objective: Resume productive doses after review and apply an identified force/redirection need.
weeks.progression: Restoration is a change; directional variation requires a reason and its own baseline.
weeks.assessment: Check tolerance to restored workload and any newly chosen direction before adding further demand.

weeks.title: Develop force or information
weeks.objective: Develop a selected strength, approach or cue-choice demand while retaining complementary output.
weeks.progression: No simultaneous growth of approach speed, decision difficulty, impact dose and strength load.
weeks.assessment: Record the limiting factor and actual response; alternate developmental and lighter routes for frequent attendance.

weeks.title: Make development repeatable
weeks.objective: Consolidate useful loads and redirection; conditionally organize linked contacts without increasing impact volume.
weeks.progression: Repeatability leads; a rebound branch requires landing/rhythm competence and no contact increase.
weeks.assessment: Review fatigue across actual visits and sport, including grip/shoulder demands before tumbling.

weeks.title: Verify readiness to apply
weeks.objective: Review like-for-like output and establish eligibility for selected application tasks.
weeks.progression: Retention, comparison or recovery; a later phase does not confer cue/rebound eligibility.
weeks.assessment: Review each current branch and record whether continued simple practice is the best next step.

weeks.title: Apply established capacity
weeks.objective: Apply known movement to justified start cues, directions or constrained partner information.
weeks.progression: One information/task change or restoration; maintain strength foundations.
weeks.assessment: Record whether the added information improves a useful task without degrading control or spacing.

weeks.title: Refine the useful application
weeks.objective: Improve an established application or one strength anchor according to the athlete's remaining need.
weeks.progression: Do not escalate all tasks because the block is nearing completion.
weeks.assessment: Separate response errors from movement errors; preserve the same comparison conditions.

weeks.title: Retain output and readiness
weeks.objective: Repeat representative work while managing fatigue ahead of the final review and current sport demands.
weeks.progression: Hold useful effort/skill; reduce surplus work when justified, without a compulsory taper.
weeks.assessment: No last-minute novel tasks or hidden test rehearsals; identify records needed for the handoff.

weeks.title: Verify and carry forward
weeks.objective: Document current competencies, productive doses, review response and a conditional next-block plan.
weeks.progression: Compare familiar tasks and preserve useful anchors; no compulsory maximum test or beginner restart.
weeks.assessment: Record both recent productive and latest review work, actual attendance and sport context; make up missed observations within later normal visits.

methods.quality_attempts: Fully recovered quality attempts; task-appropriate readiness governs restart. Descriptive intent, not an approved method-card ID.
methods.strength_sets: Controlled straight strength sets with planned reserve and task-appropriate recovery; no routine failure or maximal test.
methods.noncompeting_pairs: Optional noncompeting pairs only when local fatigue, attention, equipment and timing preserve both tasks' recovery.
methods.technical_practice: Concise purposeful rehearsal and feedback within the component clock; lower physical demand for instruction.
methods.comparable_observation: Observation under recorded matching conditions replaces equivalent training efforts or sets rather than adding test volume.

sessions.title: Continue and calibrate: Acceleration and knee-pattern strength
sessions.primary_objective: Carry the established short acceleration into this block.
sessions.quality_target: Reproduce the familiar start and run through the endpoint with a controlled runoff; record comparable efforts without chasing a best time.
sessions.maintenance_qualities: Qualified speed/output, broad strength, usable range, balance/coordination, participation and separate body-control continuity at doses appropriate to actual attendance; tags do not multiply exposure.
sessions.explosive_focus: Retain the known start, distance and recovered-attempt dose; calibrate only uncertain conditions.
sessions.strength_emphasis: Knee-pattern lead; hip, push, pull and brace complement the day.
sessions.strength_decision: Retain the last productive knee-pattern variation, working dose and effort; the latest light review is context, not the sole baseline.
sessions.progression_rationale: A usable opening comparison and productive familiar work preserve continuity while revealing changed readiness.
sessions.retained_qualities: Retain productive qualified variants except the day's specifically justified branch change; retain adequate recovery, controlled positions, complementary full-body exposure and the separate tumbling booking.
sessions.prerequisite: Qualified start and effort level, lane/stop cues and controlled runoff; demonstrated knee/hip, push/pull and brace variations. A new start or longer run needs its own check.

progression_gate.ready: Apply only the day's stated conditional change after the relevant actual prior prescription was repeatable at its quality/effort target and current recovery, equipment and space permit it. A planned day reference is not proof of completion.
progression_gate.partial: Hold the last demonstrated dose/variation, refine the limiting cue or reduce the limiting demand; do not advance other variables to compensate.
progression_gate.fatigued: Retain a familiar shorter or lower-intent acceleration rehearsal and controlled stopping, with fewer demanding efforts. Use familiar lower-demand knee/hip and supported upper-body work; no distance, load or complexity increase.
progression_gate.missed: Use the most recent actual relevant exposure and necessary calibration. No make-up attempts/sets and no calendar-based advancement.
progression_gate.new_entrant: Use demonstrated on-ramp competencies and the qualified variation at an appropriate entry dose within today's current offering; retain mastered domains and remediate only gaps.
progression_gate.stop: Stop or modify for pain, dizziness, distress, restrictions or materially altered mechanics according to the existing facility/professional procedure; this plan does not grant clearance.

preparation.base: Full/compact familiar Vortex base, including concluding hinge and squat checks; use qualified drill variants.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse the start's foot pressure, projection and trunk organization; use the base squat/hinge checks to confirm strength positions.
Progressively rehearse the selected acceleration over a controllable portion of the verified lane, including the stop/runoff.

sessions.complementarity: Acceleration goes first to protect output. Knee-pattern strength develops general force capacity; hip and upper-body work maintain a broad visit without claiming direct sprint transfer. Pair a lead lift only with a task that does not share its limiting tissues or disrupt rest.
sessions.workload_emphasis: Running efforts/distance and leg force are the main athletic demand. Count start rehearsals separately by effort; strength and subsequent tumbling add leg exposure even when exercise names differ.

recovery.development_route: D: development eligible only after completed-exposure and total-load review. Use the chosen primary change or retention plan, not maximal development of every anchor.
recovery.lighter_route: Retain a familiar shorter or lower-intent acceleration rehearsal and controlled stopping, with fewer demanding efforts. Use familiar lower-demand knee/hip and supported upper-body work; no distance, load or complexity increase.
recovery.density_rule: Do not progress quality output by shortening required recovery; lane turnover is not automatically individual recovery.

assessment.purpose: Comparable opening observations replace some work; actual prior-block history is required for individual continuation.
assessment.conditions: Record exact variant/branch, implement/load, distance, surface, effort category, rest and scoring method. Changed conditions qualify or reset comparisons. Never fabricate gains or actual results.
assessment.accounting: Observation replaces equivalent training work; no extra test sets or finisher attempts.

sessions.final_window: Recovery, low-fatigue coaching and readiness handoff inside the allotted 15/5 minutes; any scored output stays inside the explosive dose. No hidden hard conditioning or additional impact work ahead of tumbling.

tumbling.interface: Communicate running and knee-pattern leg demand and all preparation/landing exposure. Prefer the already qualified body-control lane; the separate coach checks landing and support readiness before choosing its dose.

sessions.compressed_priority: Preserve primary recovered starts and the lead knee exposure; first remove optional secondary running and redundant strength sets. Retain modest hip, push, pull and brace roles and the scheduled tumbling block.

attendance.one_or_two_visits: Take D if recovered regardless of weekday, retain broad strength and replace secondary work within time if actual coverage needs a familiar anchor.
attendance.consecutive_visits: Start from D/L alternation; three or five visits may use D/L/D or D/L/D/L/D only with recovery and sport-calendar review. L is a specific later prescription, not permission for five hard sessions.
attendance.on_ramp_rule: Directly observed competence can bypass instruction; family entry unlocks only the qualified variation, not advanced cue, rebound, running or tumbling tasks.

entry_alternative.primary_objective: Produce a familiar controlled throw while landing competency is still instructional; no jump-output outcome is claimed.
entry_alternative.quality_target: Use the qualified stable stance, release only into the clear designated space and retrieve only on permission; keep the known projection coordinated without a loss of balance.
entry_alternative.prerequisite: Separately passed throw handling, stance, release direction, retrieval and conduct checks (OR-05/09/19 or direct evidence), with appropriate upper-body readiness. OR-06 landing/hinge checks alone do not establish throwing eligibility, and neither does a failed landing check.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse the qualified stable throwing stance, trunk/shoulder organization and hip control relevant to the later hinge.
Progressively rehearse the familiar throw toward a clear target with controlled release and retrieval; no jumping is required.
entry_alternative.progression: Use the actual last passed throw and appropriate entry dose; retain implement, stance, direction and effort while participation is calibrated. The day's jump direction/rebound/contact progression does not apply. At the next JUMP family visit, retain or develop this throw only from its actual response, or select a jump only after a separate landing check.
entry_alternative.strength: Keep the day's qualified hip lead and complementary full-body roles; hold a proposed hip progression during first-visit branch calibration, and reduce push/throw work if shoulder readiness requires it.
entry_alternative.accounting: Select JUMP-T instead of JUMP and its complementary THROW allocation; prescribe one primary throw allocation, not two. Record throws and actual effort, not jump contacts or a jump comparison. Any non-flight landing instruction is separately identified practice within time.
entry_alternative.workload_emphasis: Primary explosive exposure is throwing. No unqualified flight is added; record any actual preparation/support, strength and separate tumbling demands independently.
entry_alternative.tumbling: Report the unresolved landing competency and throw/shoulder work; the separate coach selects only the independently qualified body-control lane.
entry_alternative.compressed: Protect the one primary throwing task and recovery; no secondary output task is required. Retain appropriate hip/knee/push/pull/brace roles and the normal clocks.
entry_alternative.identity_status: provisional_delivery_branch; exact throw/cue variant approval pending
entry_alternative.precedence: When selected, this branch replaces the regular primary objective, explosive task, its two targeted drills, complementary throwing allocation and D/L recovery route. It retains the component clocks and qualified full-body roles.

recovery.development_route: Use the separately passed stationary throw/cue at an appropriate entry dose and this branch's quality target; main jumping/traveling progressions do not apply.
recovery.lighter_route: Retain only a passed stationary stance/throw or early cue at lower demand with fewer demanding throws, or omit throwing if shoulder, trunk, attention or symptoms make it inappropriate. Do not send the athlete into the unqualified jump/travel domain as the lighter alternative. Keep qualified strength/foundational practice or defer the affected work.

entry_alternative.base_override: Keep the recognizable full/compact base and concluding hinge/squat checks. Where landing/flight remains unqualified, use passed non-flight march/ankling and landing-position practice instead of unqualified skip/pogo/jump exposure; qualified unaffected base tasks remain available. Resolve exact age prescriptions later.

sessions.title: Continue and calibrate: Branch-specific running and balanced strength
sessions.primary_objective: Establish comparable upright running output in a verified runway, or a separately identified short-start baseline.
sessions.quality_target: RUN-U: repeat the established buildup and upright zone without reaching or straining. RUN-S: repeat a short acceleration and safe stop; do not score it as upright speed.
sessions.maintenance_qualities: Qualified speed/output, broad strength, usable range, balance/coordination, participation and separate body-control continuity at doses appropriate to actual attendance; tags do not multiply exposure.
sessions.explosive_focus: Choose RUN-U only after runway verification; hold the known running task. If unavailable, select RUN-S and open its own comparison history.
sessions.strength_emphasis: Balanced full-body strength with modest knee lead and hip/push/pull/brace support.
sessions.strength_decision: Retain balanced lower-body work with a modest lead knee-pattern role; retain push, pull and brace without a load test.
sessions.progression_rationale: A stable setup is necessary for useful comparison; the facility branch changes the delivered outcome and must remain visible.
sessions.retained_qualities: Retain productive qualified variants except the day's specifically justified branch change; retain adequate recovery, controlled positions, complementary full-body exposure and the separate tumbling booking.
sessions.prerequisite: RUN-U needs a verified buildup, usable upright zone, runoff, surface and qualified action. RUN-S needs a verified short lane and stopping skill. Both use appropriately qualified full-body strength. Rhythm drills alone do not qualify or deliver maximal velocity.

progression_gate.ready: Apply only the day's stated conditional change after the relevant actual prior prescription was repeatable at its quality/effort target and current recovery, equipment and space permit it. A planned day reference is not proof of completion.
progression_gate.partial: Hold the last demonstrated dose/variation, refine the limiting cue or reduce the limiting demand; do not advance other variables to compensate.

preparation.base: Full/compact familiar Vortex base, including concluding hinge and squat checks; use qualified drill variants.

sessions.quality_target: An eligible rebound remains low, coordinated and controlled at exit; a jump-and-stick athlete repeats a balanced landing instead.
sessions.maintenance_qualities: Qualified speed/output, broad strength, usable range, balance/coordination, participation and separate body-control continuity at doses appropriate to actual attendance; tags do not multiply exposure.
sessions.explosive_focus: For qualified athletes with a reason to link contacts, replace selected isolated efforts with a brief linked task; keep total demanding contacts no greater and do not raise height/distance.
sessions.strength_emphasis: Hip-pattern lead; modest knee, push, pull and brace roles.
sessions.strength_decision: Hold hinge dose and load; reduce nonessential lower-body work if the new contact organization changes tolerance.
sessions.progression_rationale: Rebound organization is a conditional task change, not permission to add contacts or force every athlete off a useful stick landing.
sessions.retained_qualities: Retain productive qualified variants except the day's specifically justified branch change; retain adequate recovery, controlled positions, complementary full-body exposure and the separate tumbling booking.
sessions.prerequisite: Control the selected jump landing and exit; linked contacts require demonstrated low-rebound rhythm and landing tolerance. A directional jump has its own competency check. Use qualified hip, knee and upper-body variations.

progression_gate.ready: Apply only the day's stated conditional change after the relevant actual prior prescription was repeatable at its quality/effort target and current recovery, equipment and space permit it. A planned day reference is not proof of completion.
progression_gate.partial: Hold the last demonstrated dose/variation, refine the limiting cue or reduce the limiting demand; do not advance other variables to compensate.
progression_gate.fatigued: Use familiar low-demand takeoff/landing practice with fewer contacts and no new rebound or direction; retain a small familiar throw only if shoulder readiness permits. Keep full-body strength familiar with reduced demanding work.
progression_gate.missed: Use the most recent actual relevant exposure and necessary calibration. No make-up attempts/sets and no calendar-based advancement.
progression_gate.new_entrant: Use demonstrated on-ramp competencies and the qualified variation at an appropriate entry dose within today's current offering; retain mastered domains and remediate only gaps.
progression_gate.stop: Stop or modify for pain, dizziness, distress, restrictions or materially altered mechanics according to the existing facility/professional procedure; this plan does not grant clearance.

anchor_roles.name: Throwing entry instead of an unqualified jump

preparation.base: Full/compact familiar Vortex base, including concluding hinge and squat checks; use qualified drill variants.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse the selected takeoff/landing position and hip/trunk organization; relate it to the day's hinge and the base hinge/squat observations.
Build progressively into the selected jump task at controllable amplitude; use a stick variant until rebound prerequisites are demonstrated.

sessions.complementarity: The primary jump comes before fatigue. A familiar throw supplies complementary upper-body explosive work only if its setup and shoulder demand fit. Hinge strength develops force capacity; avoid adding several near-identical jump drills to fill the window. Separate grip-limited hinges and pulls if pairing would compromise either.
sessions.workload_emphasis: Separate takeoffs/landings by task, direction and isolated/rebound demand; include preparation and later tumbling without double counting the same event. Track throws separately from impacts and hinge sets.

recovery.development_route: D: development eligible only after completed-exposure and total-load review. Use the chosen primary change or retention plan, not maximal development of every anchor.
recovery.lighter_route: Use familiar low-demand takeoff/landing practice with fewer contacts and no new rebound or direction; retain a small familiar throw only if shoulder readiness permits. Keep full-body strength familiar with reduced demanding work.
recovery.density_rule: Do not progress quality output by shortening required recovery; lane turnover is not automatically individual recovery.

assessment.purpose: Review fatigue across actual visits and sport, including grip/shoulder demands before tumbling.
assessment.conditions: Record exact variant/branch, implement/load, distance, surface, effort category, rest and scoring method. Changed conditions qualify or reset comparisons. Never fabricate gains or actual results.
assessment.accounting: Observation replaces equivalent training work; no extra test sets or finisher attempts.

sessions.final_window: Recovery, low-fatigue coaching and readiness handoff inside the allotted 15/5 minutes; any scored output stays inside the explosive dose. No hidden hard conditioning or additional impact work ahead of tumbling.

tumbling.interface: Share total planned and actual landing/rebound exposure plus hinge and shoulder fatigue. The separate coach may choose familiar shapes/support/orientation with fewer landings; no hidden extra impact quota.

sessions.compressed_priority: Protect the primary jump, adequate recovery and lead hinge. Remove the complementary throw first if safe setup/rest cannot fit, then redundant strength sets; keep small knee/push/pull/brace roles. No shortened-rest jump circuit.

attendance.one_or_two_visits: Take D if recovered regardless of weekday, retain broad strength and replace secondary work within time if actual coverage needs a familiar anchor.
attendance.consecutive_visits: Start from D/L alternation; three or five visits may use D/L/D or D/L/D/L/D only with recovery and sport-calendar review. L is a specific later prescription, not permission for five hard sessions.
attendance.on_ramp_rule: Directly observed competence can bypass instruction; family entry unlocks only the qualified variation, not advanced cue, rebound, running or tumbling tasks.

logistics.detailed_timing: pending Stage 3 and individual session calculations
logistics.equipment: Resolve actual implement sizes/counts, travel/runoff and safe visible work/retrieval before final selection.

entry_alternative.primary_objective: Produce a familiar controlled throw while landing competency is still instructional; no jump-output outcome is claimed.
entry_alternative.quality_target: Use the qualified stable stance, release only into the clear designated space and retrieve only on permission; keep the known projection coordinated without a loss of balance.
entry_alternative.prerequisite: Separately passed throw handling, stance, release direction, retrieval and conduct checks (OR-05/09/19 or direct evidence), with appropriate upper-body readiness. OR-06 landing/hinge checks alone do not establish throwing eligibility, and neither does a failed landing check.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse the qualified stable throwing stance, trunk/shoulder organization and hip control relevant to the later hinge.
Progressively rehearse the familiar throw toward a clear target with controlled release and retrieval; no jumping is required.
entry_alternative.progression: Use the actual last passed throw and appropriate entry dose; retain implement, stance, direction and effort while participation is calibrated. The day's jump direction/rebound/contact progression does not apply. At the next JUMP family visit, retain or develop this throw only from its actual response, or select a jump only after a separate landing check.
entry_alternative.strength: Keep the day's qualified hip lead and complementary full-body roles; hold a proposed hip progression during first-visit branch calibration, and reduce push/throw work if shoulder readiness requires it.
entry_alternative.accounting: Select JUMP-T instead of JUMP and its complementary THROW allocation; prescribe one primary throw allocation, not two. Record throws and actual effort, not jump contacts or a jump comparison. Any non-flight landing instruction is separately identified practice within time.
entry_alternative.workload_emphasis: Primary explosive exposure is throwing. No unqualified flight is added; record any actual preparation/support, strength and separate tumbling demands independently.
entry_alternative.tumbling: Report the unresolved landing competency and throw/shoulder work; the separate coach selects only the independently qualified body-control lane.
entry_alternative.compressed: Protect the one primary throwing task and recovery; no secondary output task is required. Retain appropriate hip/knee/push/pull/brace roles and the normal clocks.
entry_alternative.identity_status: provisional_delivery_branch; exact throw/cue variant approval pending
entry_alternative.precedence: When selected, this branch replaces the regular primary objective, explosive task, its two targeted drills, complementary throwing allocation and D/L recovery route. It retains the component clocks and qualified full-body roles.

recovery.development_route: Use the separately passed stationary throw/cue at an appropriate entry dose and this branch's quality target; main jumping/traveling progressions do not apply.
recovery.lighter_route: Retain only a passed stationary stance/throw or early cue at lower demand with fewer demanding throws, or omit throwing if shoulder, trunk, attention or symptoms make it inappropriate. Do not send the athlete into the unqualified jump/travel domain as the lighter alternative. Keep qualified strength/foundational practice or defer the affected work.

entry_alternative.base_override: Keep the recognizable full/compact base and concluding hinge/squat checks. Where landing/flight remains unqualified, use passed non-flight march/ankling and landing-position practice instead of unqualified skip/pogo/jump exposure; qualified unaffected base tasks remain available. Resolve exact age prescriptions later.

adjacent_recovery.overlap: Prior offered focus: REACT; next: BRAKE. All visits can load legs, trunk and upper body; inspect actual running, impacts, plants, strength and tumbling rather than assume a new focus means recovery.
adjacent_recovery.action: If the prior actual visit was developmental and these visits are consecutive, use the suitable lighter route as the initial model. A Monday after weekend sport may also require L or time away. The family progression resumes from actual qualified work.

sessions.maintenance_qualities: Qualified speed/output, broad strength, usable range, balance/coordination, participation and separate body-control continuity at doses appropriate to actual attendance; tags do not multiply exposure.
sessions.explosive_focus: Review the known planned or cue task at a comparable approach; no new angle, speed or uncertainty is introduced for graduation.
sessions.strength_emphasis: Unilateral knee-pattern lead fills the knee role; hip, push, pull and brace support.
sessions.strength_decision: Observe familiar unilateral range and effort; record each side and any current restriction without fabricating readiness clearance.
sessions.progression_rationale: A precise qualified task is a usable starting point for the next block and for any targeted remediation.
sessions.retained_qualities: Retain productive qualified variants except the day's specifically justified branch change; retain adequate recovery, controlled positions, complementary full-body exposure and the separate tumbling booking.
sessions.prerequisite: Control a stop at the selected approach before a cut; qualify the particular angle and exit. Cue uncertainty requires an already controlled movement solution. Demonstrate the selected supported or unsupported unilateral lift on each side.

progression_gate.ready: Apply only the day's stated conditional change after the relevant actual prior prescription was repeatable at its quality/effort target and current recovery, equipment and space permit it. A planned day reference is not proof of completion.
progression_gate.partial: Hold the last demonstrated dose/variation, refine the limiting cue or reduce the limiting demand; do not advance other variables to compensate.
progression_gate.fatigued: Use a known slower planned stop or gentle redirection with fewer efforts and an unambiguous cue. Use supported unilateral control at familiar light demand with hip, push/pull and brace retention; no faster approach or sharper angle.
progression_gate.missed: Use the most recent actual relevant exposure and necessary calibration. No make-up attempts/sets and no calendar-based advancement.
progression_gate.new_entrant: Use demonstrated on-ramp competencies and the qualified variation at an appropriate entry dose within today's current offering; retain mastered domains and remediate only gaps.
progression_gate.stop: Stop or modify for pain, dizziness, distress, restrictions or materially altered mechanics according to the existing facility/professional procedure; this plan does not grant clearance.

anchor_roles.name: Controlled stop / planned cut / qualified cue branch

preparation.base: Full/compact familiar Vortex base, including concluding hinge and squat checks; use qualified drill variants.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse braking foot placement and controlled hip/knee acceptance, informing the unilateral strength range as well as the plant.
Progressively rehearse the known stop or cut from an easy approach before the selected training approach; keep direction predictable during this rehearsal.

sessions.complementarity: Brake/cut practice leads while attention and leg control are fresh. Unilateral strength supplies general force/control work at a known range. A unilateral knee task fills the knee slot; do not add a second knee lift solely to tick a pattern box. Hip and upper-body work complement rather than repeat the plant stimulus.
sessions.workload_emphasis: Track approaches, hard braking plants and exits by side/direction and effort. They are not interchangeable with jump contacts. Unilateral strength, outside cutting sport and tumbling landings may overlap despite different labels.

recovery.development_route: D: development eligible only after completed-exposure and total-load review. Use the chosen primary change or retention plan, not maximal development of every anchor.
recovery.lighter_route: Use a known slower planned stop or gentle redirection with fewer efforts and an unambiguous cue. Use supported unilateral control at familiar light demand with hip, push/pull and brace retention; no faster approach or sharper angle.
recovery.density_rule: Do not progress quality output by shortening required recovery; lane turnover is not automatically individual recovery.

assessment.purpose: Record both recent productive and latest review work, actual attendance and sport context; make up missed observations within later normal visits.
assessment.conditions: Record exact variant/branch, implement/load, distance, surface, effort category, rest and scoring method. Changed conditions qualify or reset comparisons. Never fabricate gains or actual results.
assessment.accounting: Observation replaces equivalent training work; no extra test sets or finisher attempts.

sessions.final_window: Recovery, low-fatigue coaching and readiness handoff inside the allotted 15/5 minutes; any scored output stays inside the explosive dose. No hidden hard conditioning or additional impact work ahead of tumbling.

tumbling.interface: Communicate braking/plant and unilateral leg demand by side plus any control loss. The separate coach checks landing and balance readiness and can retain lower-impact foundational work.

sessions.compressed_priority: Retain the primary planned or qualified cue task and adequate approach recovery. Remove secondary directions/extra attempts before core instruction or rest; use one unilateral knee task plus small hip/push/pull/brace roles within the shortened strength window.

attendance.one_or_two_visits: Take D if recovered regardless of weekday, retain broad strength and replace secondary work within time if actual coverage needs a familiar anchor.
attendance.consecutive_visits: Start from D/L alternation; three or five visits may use D/L/D or D/L/D/L/D only with recovery and sport-calendar review. L is a specific later prescription, not permission for five hard sessions.
attendance.on_ramp_rule: Directly observed competence can bypass instruction; family entry unlocks only the qualified variation, not advanced cue, rebound, running or tumbling tasks.

logistics.equipment: Resolve actual implement sizes/counts, travel/runoff and safe visible work/retrieval before final selection.

entry_alternative.primary_objective: Recognize an early release or go/no-go cue through a familiar stationary throw while travel/braking competency is still instructional; no reactive-cut outcome is claimed.
entry_alternative.quality_target: Release only for the accepted early cue, withhold on the no-go signal when that rule is qualified, and preserve the known throwing direction, stable stance and permission-based retrieval.
entry_alternative.prerequisite: Separately passed stable throw/retrieval and early cue checks (OR-05/09/13/17 or direct evidence). A travel/cut check is not required for this stationary branch; a throw check alone does not pass a no-go rule.
targeted_drill_purposes: Rehearse the stable throwing position and shoulder/trunk control relevant to later push/pull work, including release and retrieve permission.
Progress from a predictable throw rehearsal to the athlete's passed early release/go-no-go task at controllable intent; add no traveling choice.
entry_alternative.progression: Retain the actual passed throw and early cue rule while entering the main flow; main running choice, partner-tracking or late-signal progressions do not automatically apply. At the next REACT family visit, refine this branch from actual response or move to traveling response only after its movement and cue checks are documented.
entry_alternative.strength: Retain the day's qualified push/pull emphasis and small knee/hip/brace roles, with a recoverable dose. During first-visit cue/branch calibration hold proposed upper-body progression and account for throwing plus later support load.
entry_alternative.accounting: Select REACT-T instead of traveling REACT and complementary THROW; prescribe one cue-and-throw allocation. Record cue conditions, throws and effort; no reactive running distance or braking plants are credited for this branch.
entry_alternative.workload_emphasis: Primary explosive exposure is cued throwing and upper-body/trunk work. Any qualified warm-up contacts are recorded separately; this branch receives no main reactive-running or cutting credit.
entry_alternative.tumbling: Report the unresolved travel/braking skill and throw/push/pull shoulder demand; the separate coach selects only independently qualified foundations.
entry_alternative.compressed: Retain the simple cue-and-throw task and its recovery, remove secondary output, and keep suitable full-body strength inside the compressed clock.
entry_alternative.identity_status: provisional_delivery_branch; exact throw/cue variant approval pending
entry_alternative.precedence: When selected, this branch replaces the regular primary objective, explosive task, its two targeted drills, complementary throwing allocation and D/L recovery route. It retains the component clocks and qualified full-body roles.

recovery.development_route: Use the separately passed stationary throw/cue at an appropriate entry dose and this branch's quality target; main jumping/traveling progressions do not apply.
recovery.lighter_route: Retain only a passed stationary stance/throw or early cue at lower demand with fewer demanding throws, or omit throwing if shoulder, trunk, attention or symptoms make it inappropriate. Do not send the athlete into the unqualified jump/travel domain as the lighter alternative. Keep qualified strength/foundational practice or defer the affected work.

entry_alternative.base_override: Keep the recognizable full/compact base and concluding hinge/squat checks. Where landing/flight remains unqualified, use passed non-flight march/ankling and landing-position practice instead of unqualified skip/pogo/jump exposure; qualified unaffected base tasks remain available. Resolve exact age prescriptions later.
